population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈274M. Current users: 37.6% ≈ 103.0M. Ever used: 49.0% ≈ 134.3M. Used and off now: 11.4 pts ≈ 31.2M. Never used: ≈140M. Cycling arithmetic: ever 49.0 − current 37.6 = 11.4 pts off now. About 17.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.0 pts of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (17.0+5.0)/49.0 ≈ 45% have cycled. Ever-use rose 13.5 pts, inside the 15.6 limit, and current use rose 12.6, so the 2033–34 growth mixes new users with people coming back. Three groups came back. Lapsed injectable users restarted on the 50 mg Wegovy pill. Users dropped by employers moved to cash portals or imports. Drinkers came in through the alcohol-use-disorder guideline route. This mix fits the parent's ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% one-year restart rate. Age check: 18–29 at 25% × 52M = 13.0M; 30–49 at 44% × 91M = 40.0M; 50–64 at 51% × 61M = 31.1M; 65+ at 27% × 70M = 18.9M; total ≈ 103.0M. The 18–29 band nearly doubled for three reasons: $149 orals, $5–30 imported pills and pens, and AUD-route prescribing. The 65+ band grew more slowly than total use because DEXA pauses and the NAION warning (older, diabetic users carry the most risk) hold it back; about one 65+ ever-user in five is off on a medically advised pause. Income thirds average ≈37.7, so they bracket the national rate. The bottom third rose from 21% to 31% through four more Medicaid adopter states and through imports. About 10.5M import and counterfeit users are under-measured and skew to the bottom and middle thirds. The top third is the most likely to be on 12 mg retatrutide with coaching. The off-now population (≈31M) is mostly employer drop-offs who could not afford $199–249 cash, people on bone or vision pauses, GI quitters, and people stopping by conviction. Never-users (≈140M) are now a minority among insured adults over 40 and are concentrated among under-30s, rural residents of non-adopting states, and people with contraindications. Pediatric use: 1.3% of ≈73M under-18s ≈ 950k, mostly adolescents on Medicaid EPSDT or using a parent's cash pills. The adolescent bone-accrual question is still unresolved. About one child in two lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The Part D obesity benefit is unchanged: $199/month negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, 90-day bone-pause code. From 2034 the counselling visit also asks a vision-symptom question. Medicare pays 18.3% of fills ≈ 18.8M users (17.4M aged 65+ and 1.4M disabled under-65); ≈7.0M are on for diabetes and ≈11.8M for obesity. Obesity-benefit gross: 11.8M × $199 × 12 ≈ $28.2B. Beneficiaries pay 11.8M × $50 × 12 ≈ $7.1B, leaving ≈$21.1B net to the program in 2034, about 50% above the ≈$14B/yr average in the 2031 CBO score. All Medicare incretin fills: 18.8M × $199 × 12 ≈ $44.9B gross. Medicaid: 35 states plus DC have adopted the continuation standard for the 90% match. Arizona, Georgia, Ohio and Tennessee joined in 2033, after the Seventh Circuit ruling. Medicaid pays 13.6% of fills ≈ 14.0M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $33.4B gross before supplemental rebates. The 50 mg Wegovy pill is on Part D and Medicaid formularies at the same $199 rate.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 120+ semaglutide brands, injectable at $5–30/month and generic oral semaglutide at $12–40/month (high API load). First tirzepatide copies have launched under compulsory-licence-style rulings. China: domestic semaglutide and tirzepatide generics; Chinese API underlies most of the global gray trade, including counterfeit 'Wegovy 50' tablets. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt have generics, and Mexican border pharmacies now sell generic oral semaglutide openly.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Stalled, again. The 2031 settlements set 2033 generic entry, but no generic launched. In April 2033 FDA issued complete response letters to the first semaglutide ANDA filers over peptide-related impurity and immunogenicity comparability and pen-device equivalence. Novo's suits on the 7.2 mg and device patents are pending, and one domestic filer holds only a tentative approval. Novo also put the 50 mg pill on allocation because it needs ≈20× the weekly API of an injectable. Prices: Wegovy pill and Foundayo starting doses $149, Wegovy pill 50 mg $249 on the federal direct portal (launched as TrumpRx), injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $199–279, retatrutide $399 direct and $1,499 list, amycretin $449, survodutide $429 direct. PBM net is ≈$170–190 and unchanged. Payer mix of ≈103.0M users: commercial and other, including VA/TRICARE, 24.8% (25.5M); Medicare 18.3% (18.8M); Medicaid 13.6% (14.0M); cash/direct 33.2% (34.2M, including ≈4.0M 'calm'/'focus' subscribers); imported/counterfeit 10.2% (10.5M). Sum ≈103.0M ≈100%. Covering employers fell from 66% to 44%. Most of those that still cover use code-restricted designs (type 2 diabetes, ASCVD, OSA, CKD, MASH, and increasingly AUD), and ≈80% of the rest are gated. Orals are ≈46% of all fills and ≈70% of new starts. Injectables still dominate top-efficacy use (retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin) and the import trade. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. There is no importation law.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Feb 2033 with DEXA monitoring in label)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg high dose from Feb 2033, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: MASH / liver (semaglutide; survodutide MASH data under review)
alcohol use disorder: guideline-endorsed second-line (ASAM/APA and VA/DoD, Nov 2033) for semaglutide; not FDA-labelled, sNDA filed Mar 2034 with PDUFA 2035
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol use disorder outside guideline criteria ('sober-curious' and EAP prescribing, now usually coded as AUD for coverage)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS-endpoint trial reading out 2035)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral_parity driver is met by an existing product in a new form. In Feb 2033 FDA approved a 50 mg Wegovy pill on a 72-week head-to-head trial against injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (16.6% vs 16.0% mean loss, non-inferior), with GI rates similar. The pill matches the injectables most people take. It does not match retatrutide 12 mg (≈30%), which stays the efficacy ceiling and stays an injection. Survodutide, with a PDUFA date at the start of the window, was approved Feb 2033 for chronic weight management with DEXA in the label. MariTide received a complete response letter in Jun 2033 because its 72-week DEXA substudy showed hip BMD loss beyond comparators, and Amgen plans to resubmit in 2035. Bimagrumab combinations were filed in Mar 2034, so no approval is possible before Mar 2035. AUD was realised through guidelines, and the semaglutide AUD sNDA was filed in Mar 2034. No US generic semaglutide after the April 2033 CRLs. Incretin market ≈$230B in 2034: US ≈$205B (≈92.5M paying users × ≈$185 average net × 12), ex-US ≈$25B and eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Rates on the 50 mg pill are similar to injectable semaglutide. Restart nausea after drug holidays is now a routine pharmacy complaint.
Rising in absolute numbers with high-dose retatrutide and the larger 65+ population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit cases confound reporting more than ever.
With 18.9M users aged 65+, a 2034 Medicare claims update estimates ≈1.9M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria. Survodutide's label adds a fourth lean-mass monitoring requirement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label retained. Body-composition monitoring is in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin and survodutide labels. CMS requires annual DEXA for 65+ users on therapy more than 2 years. MA strength benefits continue.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈9.0M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. At a ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × ~0.30 excess (trimmed from 0.35 by antiresorptive co-prescription), that is ≈16,000 excess hip fractures a year against ~300,000 US total, plus continuing vertebral fractures in cycling postmenopausal women aged 50–64. DEXA waits have eased to 8–14 weeks as mobile capacity grew. Employer drop-offs who lose scans entirely are a new blind spot. MariTide's CRL was the first approval decision driven by bone data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Bone endpoints are required in all filings. The CMS bone-pause code continues. Private plans remain unbound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from suspected. A 2034 FDA Sentinel pooled analysis, consistent with European registries, gives a hazard ratio of ≈1.8 across GLP-1-containing agents, highest in users over 50 with diabetes or sleep apnea. Across ≈103M users with an age-weighted baseline of ~5 per 100,000 person-years, that implies on the order of 4,000 excess cases a year if causal. Cases among imported-product users are poorly captured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions (May 2034) for all GLP-1-containing products: counsel on sudden vision loss, stop promptly, and consider ophthalmic evaluation in high-risk patients. The EMA aligned from 'very rare'. The Part D counselling template adds a vision question. FAA AME guidance adds visual-field review for pilots on GLP-1s.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retatrutide SHAPS data hold at ~12% of 12 mg users versus ~5% of comparators. A 2034 university survey linked to pharmacy claims found ~8% of low-dose 'calm' subscribers above threshold versus ~5% of matched non-users. It is the first independent low-dose measurement, it is not randomised, and it is contested.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders stand. No label change. FDA asked the AUD sNDA sponsor for SHAPS data.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Larger again. Employer retreat in the 2034 plan year pushed several million people off coverage. Most moved to cash or imports, but those who could not pay are producing a wave of regain episodes.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver (Oct 2033) but required a clinician-certified medical-pause exception.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency are common in high-loss older users and in unsupervised import users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance and the Part D counselling screen. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of follow-up. The adolescent bone-accrual signal persists in a subset of rapid losers, and the sample is still small. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Full adolescent data due to FDA in 2034, with the review ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Now a public-health story. Aug–Oct 2033: counterfeit pens containing insulin and contaminated 'research peptide' vials caused ≈600 hospitalisations (severe hypoglycaemia, sepsis, abscesses) and 19 deaths across 14 states. Counterfeit 'Wegovy 50' tablets with 0–3× labelled dose are circulating. Poison-centre calls are up ~60% from 2032 as import users rose from ≈3.8M to ≈10.5M.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Alert Network notice. CBP seizures roughly tripled. FDA added authentication QR codes to its BeSafeRx campaign. The 'Safe Pens' bill passed the House and stalled in the Senate. Individuals are still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Higher fall-related ED visits persist in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. The vision warning adds a new line to fall-risk screening.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening is mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Employer retreat added a large new cohort of involuntary cyclers aged 45–64. DEXA cohorts continue to show less lean mass and more visceral fat at the same weight.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Covered in the 2034 joint guidance; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide and a smaller rise with survodutide; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled as a precaution; retatrutide cardiovascular outcomes trial to read out 2035.

food_and_beverage.state: With nearly four adults in ten on the drug, salty snacks fall ~5% a year and confectionery ~6%. A third major group has exited candy. Daily pills spread on-plan eating to under-30s, and convenience-store 'pill-friendly' mini-meal formats are now the growth segment. Fortified 'bone-forward' dairy and protein lines still lead.

alcohol.state: Seventh straight year of spirits volume decline, now steeper as AUD prescribing becomes guideline practice. Kentucky distillers in Bardstown and Louisville cut warehouse shifts and stretch ageing inventory. Beer and wine are also down, while non-alcoholic and 'one good drink' formats keep growing. Brewers sponsor 'drug-holiday weekend' events.

restaurants.state: Spend per cover is down ~10–12% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Half portions and gram pricing are universal. 'Full table' nights and heritage rooms in Atlanta, Memphis and Houston do best on Friday and Saturday, when holiday-takers show up.

apparel.state: Employer retreat triggered a visible regain wave among 45–64-year-olds in 2034. Resale and cycling-sized rental grew, and mid-market brands keep inventory deliberately thin across sizes.

fitness.state: DEXA-plus-coaching chains and MA 'prescribed lifting' keep expanding. Mobile DEXA capacity eased waits, and staffing for older lifters is still the constraint.

insurance.state: Employers covering weight management fell from 66% to 44% after pharmacy trend ran ~+7–9% on volume at flat prices and the 2033 generic did not come. Coverage now runs mostly through diabetes, cardiac, OSA, CKD, MASH and AUD codes. Many employers that stopped paying kept outcomes-based wellness discounts, rewarding employees who upload kiosk weights and cash pharmacy claims. Life insurers keep the 'why untreated' question.

pharma.state: Volume rose ~50% at flat prices. Novo gained back share through the 50 mg pill but is constrained by API supply and spending heavily on peptide plants in North Carolina and Denmark. Lilly holds the top tier with retatrutide 12 mg and Foundayo. Indian and Chinese generic makers win abroad and indirectly supply the US gray market. Ophthalmology and DEXA makers are winners.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Fully normalised, and now invisible. With pills, nobody sees an injection. 'On' is the default assumption at any adult table in Dublin, Ohio or Gilbert, Arizona. 'Off' needs a reason: bone pause, eye scare, 'my job dropped it', or 'by conviction'. Visible regain at 50 is read as an employer change.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use levels converge (bottom third 31%, top 43%), and quality of care splits harder. Top-third users run 12 mg retatrutide with coaching, DEXA and antiresorptives. The middle pays $199–249 cash for pills with no scans. The bottom relies on Medicaid kiosks or $20 Indian pills by mail with no oversight. In Phoenix, a mailed blister pack with Devanagari print is a recognised working-class object.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Hosts plan for 'on' guests by default. Friday and Saturday 'holiday dinners', timed to Foundayo weekends, are a new informal ritual among under-40s. Church potlucks and no-gram rooms remain deliberate heritage.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: The on/off field on apps is now near-universal. 'Holiday-compatible' (shared weekends off) is a stated preference. 'Unmedicated' stays a niche filter, mostly in Atlanta and Austin.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Assumed to be managed. Since the AUD guideline, the same is assumed for craving in general, so a second drink now prompts a question. The Atlanta and Tulsa–Dallas backlash coalition is proportionally smaller still. It is now aligned with disability lawyers on 'weigh-in welfare' and with families of counterfeit victims.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. About 9M Americans are on top-dose triple or dual regimens. At ~12% versus ~5% SHAPS threshold crossing, that implies roughly 600k excess cases of clinically meaningful anhedonia if causal. The first independent low-dose survey suggests ~8% versus ~5% among ≈4.0M 'calm' subscribers, ≈120k excess if causal, and that figure is contested. Self-reported 'grey' in a 2034 national poll: 31% of current users say it applies to them 'at least sometimes'.
interior_life.framing: A side effect everyone talks about. 'The grey' is a talk-show topic, a meme and a reason given at the pharmacy counter for stepping down a dose. 'Calm' still sells, and brands now advertise 'holiday-friendly dosing'. Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. Users schedule holidays the way they schedule haircuts.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Two large employers dropped 'focus' subscriptions from their lifestyle catalogues in 2034 after employee complaints, and the HR platform still lists them. Sales and hospitality workers take Foundayo off Thursday night to 'come back' for weekend service. Fleets and warehouses still favour continuous use, and Teamsters contracts now name vision-symptom leave alongside the bone-pause exemption.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' is reviewers' standard shorthand. Nashville and comedy circuits sell 'holiday sets' on Saturdays. Extreme sports, hot sauce and loud venues still grow. A 2034 hit TV drama centres on a family whose members are all on different doses.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples plan drug holidays for anniversaries and conception, and pharmacies sell 'restart' anti-nausea packs alongside the pills. Sex therapists routinely ask which day the last pill was taken. Counselling caseloads now include partners whose drinking stopped and whose warmth went with it.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Two fights dominate: who pays after employers walked away, and why the 2033 generic did not come. Republicans defend the continuation standard as accountability and attack FDA's CRLs as protecting Novo. Democrats call for importation of 'verified' Indian generics after the counterfeit deaths. AUD coding has become a privacy issue in custody courts and with DOT. 'Calm voter' talk remains speculation.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and cautious on peptides. It issued CRLs to the first generic semaglutide ANDAs, a CRL to MariTide on bone, the NAION class warning, and DEXA in the survodutide label. Import enforcement escalated after the counterfeit cluster (CBP seizures roughly tripled), but there are still no individual prosecutions and no importation law. The FTC keeps policing claims.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Part D obesity benefit is unchanged at $199 with a $50 copay. Medicaid's 90% match now runs in 35 states plus DC. There is no individual mandate and no federal action on employer retreat. Outcomes-based wellness incentives up to 30% of premium remain legal under the ACA/HIPAA framework, and an employer may apply them even when it does not cover the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged (≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weight, 5% at 6 months or override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+, 90-day bone pause, two misses → 6-month suspension). In 2034 CMS allowed a vision-symptom pause under the same code. The Seventh Circuit upheld Indiana's waiver (Oct 2033) with a medical-pause exception, and four more states adopted. Employer wellness programmes now ingest cash-pay pharmacy claims and kiosk weights through vendor apps. AUD-coded prescriptions appear in claims data that life insurers and DOT examiners can request.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, and fleets add vision checks after the NAION warning. FAA AMEs review visual fields for pilots on GLP-1s. The Army now accepts applicants stable on medication for 12 months, matching the Air Force, under recruiting pressure.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: High-dose oral semaglutide needs about twenty times the API of an injectable. That makes peptide API strategic and makes Novo's supply allocation political. Chinese API and Indian finished product dominate the world trade, legal and gray. The US–India framework's 'parcel cooperation' produced joint counterfeit tracing after the 2033 cluster but no legal import route. Section 232 tariffs remain.

events.event: FDA approves a 50 mg Wegovy pill after a head-to-head trial shows it matching weekly semaglutide injections (16.6% vs 16.0%); Novo prices it at $249 on the federal portal and allocates supply, citing API demand roughly twenty times that of the pen

FDA rejects the first generic semaglutide applications over peptide impurity and pen-device equivalence; the 2033 entry date set by the 2031 settlements passes with no generic on US shelves and portal prices unchanged

Benefits surveys show only 44% of employers will cover weight-loss drugs in the 2034 plan year, down from 66%; most survivors restrict coverage to diabetes, heart, sleep-apnea and kidney codes, while many keep premium discounts for workers who prove adherence at their own cost

CDC health alert after counterfeit pens filled with insulin and contaminated 'research peptide' vials cause about 600 hospitalisations and 19 deaths in 14 states; imported and counterfeit users are estimated at over 10 million

Seventh Circuit upholds Indiana's Medicaid adherence-and-weigh-in waiver but requires a medical-pause exception; Arizona, Georgia, Ohio and Tennessee adopt the CMS continuation standard within three months

FDA adds a class warning for optic-nerve stroke (NAION) to all GLP-1 drugs after a Sentinel analysis finds about 1.8 times the risk; addiction-medicine and VA guidelines endorsing semaglutide for alcohol use disorder (Nov 2033) are revised the same month to require vision counselling

open_tensions: The generic that every 2031 budget assumed did not arrive. Semaglutide ANDAs are stuck on peptide-comparability CRLs and device patents, the public bill runs ≈$45B gross in Medicare and ≈$33B in Medicaid at an unchanged $199, and ≈10.5M Americans use $5–30 imports that killed 19 people in 2033. When the generic does land, the whole public bill reprices, and the Senate has stalled on whether to authenticate imports or seal them out.

Employers stopped paying but kept watching. Workers paying $199–249 a month in cash upload kiosk weights to earn premium discounts from employers that no longer cover the drug. Their mothers on Part D have bone and vision pause codes, and the employer programmes mostly have none.

Coverage now follows diagnosis codes, and AUD has become the most flexible one. Guideline-endorsed AUD prescribing gives coverage to people whose employers dropped weight coverage, but it leaves a substance-use record that DOT examiners, life insurers and custody courts can see. The FDA AUD decision in 2035 will either formalise this route or close it.

The NAION class warning lands on ≈103M users, most of whom see no ophthalmologist. The highest-risk group (over 50, diabetic, OSA) overlaps with the bone-pause group, and import users get neither scans nor eye exams. Vision is shaping up to repeat the DEXA capacity story.
still_true: Wegovy's injectable list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, keeps the counselling visit, and keeps the 90-day 'bone pause' code.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
There is still no federal importation law, the 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand, and individuals who import pens or pills for personal use are not prosecuted.

prose.headline: The Pill Came. The Generic Didn't. Your Boss Stopped Paying. Thirty-Eight Percent of America Is On It Anyway.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 nearly four American adults in ten take an incretin drug, and most of them swallow it. The 50-milligram Wegovy pill, approved in February 2033, matched the weekly injection in a head-to-head trial, and the needle stopped being a reason to wait. Seven in ten new starts are now a tablet by the coffee maker. The only injection that still carries status is the 12-milligram retatrutide pen, which takes off almost a third of body weight and requires a bone scan every year.

Prices did not move. The 2031 settlements said generic semaglutide would arrive in 2033. In April the FDA rejected the first applications over peptide impurities and pen equivalence, and Novo's device patents are still in court. The portal price stays $149 to start and $249 for the high-dose pill. Novo rations that pill because a daily oral needs about twenty times the active ingredient of a weekly pen, and peptide supply has become a matter of national interest.

Employers drew their own conclusion. With pharmacy costs climbing on volume and no generic in sight, the share covering weight-loss drugs fell from two-thirds to under half for the 2034 plan year. The survivors mostly cover diagnoses instead: diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea, kidney disease. Many that stopped paying kept the wellness discount. A worker who uploads a kiosk weight and a cash pharmacy receipt still gets a cheaper premium, even though the company no longer buys her pills. A third of all users now pay out of pocket.

The public programmes hold the other end. Medicare's obesity benefit is still $199 with a $50 copay, and it now covers nearly nineteen million people. Medicaid's ninety-percent match runs in thirty-five states and Washington, D.C. Four more states joined after the Seventh Circuit upheld Indiana's weigh-in rules in October 2033, on the condition that a doctor can order a medical pause. The continuation standard counts pills from claims, checks weights at the pharmacy and scans older bones, and it is now ordinary. Excess hip fractures among long-term older users are estimated at about sixteen thousand a year.

The people priced out of both systems buy from abroad. More than ten million Americans now take Indian or Chinese semaglutide at five to thirty dollars a month, in blister packs or pens. In the late summer of 2033 that trade became a public-health story: pens filled with insulin and vials of contaminated 'research peptide' put about six hundred people in hospital and killed nineteen. Customs seizures tripled, and nobody was charged for personal use. The Senate is still deciding whether to verify imports or seal the mail.

In May the FDA put a warning on every GLP-1 label: the drugs nearly double the risk of a rare optic-nerve stroke. In absolute terms that is a few thousand excess cases a year across a hundred million users, concentrated in older diabetics with sleep apnea. The Part D counselling visit now asks about vision, as it asks about falls. Most users will never see an ophthalmologist, and import users see no clinician at all.

In November 2033 addiction guidelines endorsed semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, and it quickly became the most flexible code in American medicine. It gets a prescription covered when a weight code no longer does. It also leaves a substance-use record that truck-licence examiners and custody lawyers can request. Bourbon warehouses in Bardstown are cutting shifts.

The flattening is no longer marketed so much as complained about. 'The grey' comes up on talk shows and at pharmacy counters, and people plan around it. Foundayo clears in about two days, so couples skip their Thursday pill to feel things on Saturday. Restaurants fill on weekends, and comedians sell 'holiday sets'. Being on the drug is unremarkable, and being off needs an explanation, unless it is Saturday.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Peña wakes at 5:40 in Mesa and takes the 50-milligram pill with water. The rule says thirty minutes before coffee, so she sits on the edge of the tub scrolling until the timer goes. The pills cost $249, charged to her own card. The dental group dropped coverage in January. In February they emailed her the wellness app.

At the Fry's on Southern she steps onto the kiosk by the blood-pressure cuff. It reads 168.4 and shows a green check: premium discount kept, thirty-one dollars a month. She does the math in the parking lot and stops doing it.

The front desk at work smells like fluoride rinse. Dr. Shah's hygienist mentions her husband's eye thing, the warning on the box, how he's 'pausing'. Marisol says her mother paused too, for her bones, and Medicare kept her on. 'Must be nice,' says the hygienist, and nobody laughs.

At lunch she eats half a turkey wrap and saves the rest without deciding to.

Her son Tomás, nineteen, is at the kitchen table when she gets home, opening a padded envelope from Hyderabad. Twenty-two dollars for a month. She picks up the blister pack and turns it to the window, looking for the QR code the news told everyone to check. There isn't one.

'It's the same molecule, Mom.'

'The ones that killed people were the same molecule too.'

She puts it back on the table.

Thursday night she skips her pill, the way she and Ray agreed in March. On Saturday they'll drive to the Mexican place on Main, order the whole platter, and see if anything feels like anything.
